distinguishing_features: Uses a liquid-infused, low-adhesion interfacial layer rather than thermally induced spallation.
Employs an etched or plasma-treated porous surface to retain the infused liquid.
Attempts to reduce deposit-to-wall adhesion energy so ordinary flow shear can detach deposits.
Uses a process-compatible liquid film to change the fouling mechanism passively without control-loop changes.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce adhesion and accumulation of asphaltene deposits on hot crude-heat-transfer surfaces so that deposits can detach under normal flow shear without recurring shutdown-based cleaning.
parsed.viable_reason: A solvent film such as n-hexane is likely to be rapidly mixed into, displaced by, or evaporated from the hot crude stream, so the proposed persistent low-adhesion film cannot be maintained as written without replenishment or a practical barrier and retention system.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Relative to thermal cycling, applying a liquid-infused low-adhesion surface to achieve passive shear detachment is a distinct mechanism that would not be an obvious routine modification of the closest prior art.
